players.name: Josh Allen
notes: The Keep #1 · average 2.54 across 40 Superflex boards
plus: Seven-board Superflex lock: Keep #1, average 2.0.
Dual-threat floor still separates him from every other aging QB1.
minus: Turns 31 in 2026 - first real dynasty age tax on a perennial 1.01.
Yates PPR has him in the late 20s; 1QB redraft does not pay the SF premium.
grafs: Josh Allen is still the player Ball Keep is built around. Seven sources - PFN, Dynasty Nerds, FantasyPros, KeepTradeCut, and the three X experts we track - all have him inside the top four Superflex assets, and the average lands at 2.0. That is not a recency spike. It is the market admitting that a quarterback who runs, extends, and finishes in the end zone is the safest way to keep a Superflex roster relevant through 2029.

The 2025 tape is the same argument on film: launch-point throws and designed keepers, with the Bills still built to let him create when protection breaks. Redraft boards (Field Yates has him in the high 20s) treat him as a mid QB1 because 1QB leagues do not have to pay the second-starter tax. Dynasty Superflex does. That split is the whole point of The Keep.

The minus is honest: he will be 31 this season, and the first time a 23-year-old passer (Maye) outranks him on a short list, the age conversation gets louder. We are not selling the 1.01 for that. We are naming it. If you are rebuilding past 2028, Maye is the bet. If you are trying to win the next two title windows, Allen is still the chip you do not put in a trade calculator for fun.

Standard scoring bumps him even further. The 238-yard game we clipped from 2025 is not a meme week; it is the ceiling that makes managers ignore every 'running backs don't last' sermon for one more startup.

What the experts are buying is the complete profile: between-the-tackles power, speed to the edge, and enough routes to keep him on the field on third down. At 24 he is still on the young side of a feature back's prime. That is rare in a 2026 running-back market full of 27-year-old win-now names.

The honest minus is architecture. Atlanta can become a game-script problem, and Superflex drafters who believe Maye/Allen/Chase are less replaceable will let Bijan slide one spot. If you are in 1QB or a redraft league that rewards rushing volume, do not overthink it. He is a first-round pick with a younger age curve than CMC, Henry, or Barkley.

The 2025 Can't-Miss play - 63 yards of broken tackles - is the scouting report: speed, strength, and a refusal to be brought down by the first or second man.

Where boards disagree is not talent, it is format. Erickson sliding him to eight is a Superflex tell: some experts will take Daniels/Herbert before they take a receiver. PPR redraft loves him even more than dynasty does, because you do not have to save a slot for a second passer.

The minus is Cincinnati's quarterback room, not Chase. If Burrow misses time, the weekly floor dips and the 'is this still a WR1 week?' tweets start. Dynasty can live through that. Redraft feels it immediately. We are not fading the player. We are fading the injury news cycle around the person throwing him the ball.
